DACONO PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OP!NION NO. 58 s. MAY 15 2025 HON. CATTLEYA M. SO Municipal Mayor Matnog, Sorsogon Dear Mayor So: We write in reference to your earlier letter requesting this Department's review and legal opinion on the validity of the following issuances issued by the Province of Sorsogon, to wit: 1. Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution No. 165-20231 rendering null and void Matnog Municipal Ordinance No. 2023-02. 2. Provincial Government of Sorsogon Office Order No. 71-20232 ordering the assignment of certain personnel of the province to look into the financial situation of the LGUs of Matnog, Gubat and Bulan. In the said letter, it is submitted that the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Matnog enacted Ordinance No. 2023-02 charging an environmental fee to all passengers bound for Visayas and Mindanao. Upon review, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Sorsogon passed a resolution rendering said ordinance null and void premised on the following grounds: 1. The stated coverage under Section 4 or the ordinance must be applicable to all, not only to passengers going to Visayas and Mindanao in line with the equal protection clause. 2. As it affects the riding public, public consultation should have been held especially to those directly affected, i.e., passengers, drivers and travelers bound for Visayas and Mindanao. 3. By definition, environmental fees are meant to defray the costs associated with disposing of the waste, fluid, failed parts, tires and other hazardous materials. Environmental fee means the fee established to provide for the costs of administering programs for the reduction, reuse and recycling of waste produced by littering, failing to reuse or recycle or other actions or inactions by 1 Resolution Declaring Invalid the Matnog Municipal Ordinance No. 2023-02 Entitled: An Ordinance Charging Environmental Fee to All Passengers Bound for Visayas and Mindanao. 2 Ordering Certain Personnel of PTO, PACCO, OPPDC and PBO to Assist the LGUs of Matnog, Gubat and Bulan and To Look into Their Financial Situation and for Other Purposes. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

individuals. Considering that the utilization of funds provided in the subject ordinance are already incorporated or included in the basic services of the LGU with proper appropriation thereof, the same is redundant and superfluous. Perforce, the LGU of Matnog and the Provincial Government of Sorsogon have already forged a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the same purpose as that of the subject ordinance in the KALINIGAN project of the 7K Program. You are of the view that the grounds relied upon by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in disapproving the ordinance are not in accordance with Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. Meanwhile, you are of the view that Office Order No. 71-2023 encroaches on your power as Local Chief Executive to assign personnel in your offices. You further state that ordering certain personnel from the Provincial Treasurer's Office, Provincial Accountant Office (PACCO), Provincial Planning and Development Office and Provincial Budget Office to assist and look into the financial situation of your municipality is not within the ambit of the power of supervision exercise by the Provincial Government over the municipalities within its territorial jurisdiction. First, on the validity of Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution No. 165-2023, we respectfully submit that the validity of legislative enactments lies with the judiciary and not with this Department. Be that as it may, for your information and guidance only, we invite your attention to the discussion below: We find Section 56 (c) ofthe Local Government Code of 1991 (hereinafter, the "Code") instructive, thus: SECTION 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (c) If the Sangguniang Panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concemed, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. It is clear from the foregoing that the only ground to declare an ordinance or resolution invalid, in whole or in part, is when the same is beyond the power conferred upon the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan concerned. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 23, series of 2013, we had the opportunity to state that: aside from the fact that the sangguniang panlalawigan is bound to limit its review of the appropriation ordinance to the requirements set forth by the aforementioned provisions of the Code, Section 56(c) thereof is clear in providing for the only ground upon which a city ordinance or resolution may be declared invalid by the sangguniang panlalawigan i.e., the ordinance is beyond the power conferred upon the sanggunian concemed. Page 2 of 4

In relation thereto, the case of Moday vs. CA (G.R. No. 107916, 20 February 1997) is instructive. In the said case, the Supreme Court, citing Velasco vs. Blas (G.R. No. [-30456, 20 July 1982) ruled that: 'The only ground upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, ordinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance or order is beyond the power conferred upon the council or president making the same'. Absolutely, no other is recognized by the law. A strictly legal question is before the provincial board in its consideration of a municipal resolution, ordinance or order. The provincial (board's) disapproval of any resolution, ordinance or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance, or order is outside the scope of the legal powers conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limits, it usurps the legislative functions of the municipal council, or president. Such has been consistent course of executive authority. " As to the second issue, may we direct your attention to Section 25 (a) of the Code regarding the relationship between the province over its component cities and municipalities is one of general supervision, not of control, thus: SECTION 25 National Supervision over Local Govemment Units. - (a) Consistent with the basic policy on local autonomy, the President shall exercise general supervision over local govemment units to ensure that their acts are within the scope of their prescribed powers and functions. The President shall exercise supervisory authority directly over provinces, highly urbanized cities, and independent component cities; through the province with respect to component cities and municioalities: and through the city and municipality with respect to Barangays. Clearly, the foregoing provision only allows supervision and proscribes control. The rationale behind this limitation is understood to be for the purpose of ensuring that municipalities act upon their defined constitutional and legislative mandates. In Drilon v. Lima, the Supreme Court distinguished the term control and supervision, "the first being the power of an officer to alter or modify or set aside what a subordinate officer had done in the performance of his duties and to substitute the judgement of the former for the latter, while the second is the power of a superior officer to see to it that lower officers perform their functions in accordance with law". Thus, along this line, the Department is of considered view that the assignment personnel of the Provincial Government to examine the financial situation of the concerned municipalities is not valid as this goes beyond purely supervisory authority. 3 G.R. No. 112497, 04 August 1994 Page 3 of 4

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/jvpr/clp Copy furnished: ATTY. ARNALDO E.
